facts.statement: Unlike other therizinosaurs, the claws of Therizinosaurus were very straight, compressed laterally, and curved only at the tips.

facts.statement: The tibia of Therizinosaurus was stocky and robust, being widest at its lower end.

facts.statement: Unlike most theropods, the first toe of Therizinosaurus was functional and weight-bearing, despite being shorter than the other toes.

facts.statement: The genus was assigned to its own family, Therizinosauridae, because it differed significantly from other known taxa.

facts.statement: In 1997, Russell coined the infraorder Therizinosauria to contain all segnosaurs.

facts.statement: Therizinosaurus possessed large, well-developed arms, a robust pelvic girdle suited for sitting, and a robust, shortened hindlimb structure.

facts.statement: Maleev described the genus Therizinosaurus in 1954, initially hypothesizing that its large claws were used to harvest seaweed.
facts.quote: When the genus was first described by Maleev in 1954, he considered that the unusually large claws were used to harvest seaweed.

facts.statement: Rozhdestvensky suggested in 1970 that the claws might have been used to open termite mounds or for a fruit-eating diet.

facts.statement: Barsbold proposed in 1976 that the claws were used to impale prey or dig, though he noted they were fragile under impact.

facts.statement: Nessov suggested in 1995 that the claws served for defense and that juveniles might have used them for climbing like modern sloths.
facts.quote: In 1995, Lev A. Nessov suggested the elongated claws were used for defense against predators and juveniles could have used their claws for arboreal locomotion, in a similar way to the modern-day sloths or hoatzin chicks.

facts.statement: Digital simulations by Lautenschlager indicated that the curved claws of Therizinosaurus were poorly suited for scratching or digging.
facts.quote: Lautenschlager noted the more strongly curved and elongate claws of some therizinosaurian taxa were poorly functional in a scratch/digging fashion, indicating this as the most unlikely function.

facts.statement: Research suggests Therizinosaurus likely used its hands in a hook-and-pull motion to grasp vegetation rather than for digging.
facts.quote: Instead of being used for fossorial behavior, it is more likely that Therizinosaurus make use of its hands in a hook-and-pull fashion to pull or grasp vegetation within reach.

facts.statement: Measurements in 2018 showed that the arm bones of Therizinosaurus were resilient enough to generate significant forces.
facts.quote: Scott A. Lee and Zachary Richards in 2018 based on bending resistance measurements of several dinosaur humeri, found the humeri of carnosaur, therizinosaur, and tyrannosaur dinosaurs to be relatively resilient to stress.

facts.statement: A 2023 study suggests the claws of Therizinosaurus may have been merely decorative and a result of growth rather than having a mechanical function.
facts.quote: A 2023 study by Qin, Rayfield, Benton, et al., regarding the claw function in therizinosaurids and alvarezsaurids, which represent the extremes of theropod claw morphology, suggest that there was no mechanical function identifiable for Therizinosaurus, suggesting the claws on its forelimbs were merely decorative rather than functional and a result of peramorphic growth resulting from increased body size.

facts.statement: Fossils of Therizinosaurus have been found in the Nemegt Formation of the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: The remains of Therizinosaurus have been found in the well-known Nemegt Formation of the Gobi Desert.

facts.statement: The age of the Nemegt Formation is estimated to be Late Campanian to Maastrichtian based on fossil assemblages, despite lacking radiometric dates.
facts.quote: Although this formation has never been dated radiometrically because of the discontinuity of exposures and absence of datable volcanic rock facies, the vertebrate fossil assemblage suggests a Maastrichtian stage (and possibly Late Campanian).

facts.statement: The climate where Therizinosaurus lived was temperate with monsoons, temperatures between 7.6 and 8.7 °C, and annual rainfall between 775 and 835 mm.
facts.quote: The climate of the formation was relatively temperate (mean annual temperatures between 7.6 and 8.7 °C), characterized by monsoons with cold, dry winters and hot, rainy summers with the addition of mean annual precipitations between 775 mmm and 835 mmm, a precipitation that was subject to prominent seasonal fluctuations.

facts.statement: Therizinosaurus lived in environments featuring large rivers and extensive Araucaria forests.

facts.statement: Therizinosaurus was one of the tallest dinosaurs in the Nemegt Formation due to its high-browsing lifestyle.
